site.name: harborwallet-mobile
site.summary: harborwallet-mobile Fictional consumer wallet "Harbor Wallet" iOS-style phone fixture. Single-page app simulating a 390 × 844 device frame with notch, status bar, home indicator, and tab bar. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - **Phone chassis** — 12 px chrome + radial gradient backdrop. Renders edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px viewport). - **Status bar** — live ticking time (rounded down to minutes), signal bars, wifi, battery (78%). - **Tab bar** (bottom) — 5 tabs: Home / Send / Receive / Activity / Account. explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full harborwallet-mobile system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Harbor Wallet mobile app demonstrates functional numeric input and clear visual hierarchy in the 'Send' flow, but suffers from critical validation gaps and accessibility issues. Users can enter amounts vastly exceeding their balance without immediate error feedback, and key interactive elements (quick-select chips, header icons) fall below standard mobile tap-target guidelines, increasing the risk of mis-taps.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore the Harbor Wallet mobile fixture, focusing on the Account/Settings flow (specifically Privacy), validating core transactional paths (Send/Receive), and critiquing UX accessibility issues identified in the prescan.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will begin by establishing the baseline Home state, then navigate to the 'Account' tab to locate and exercise the Settings/Privacy controls. It will subsequently validate the primary 'Send' and 'Receive' flows to ensure functional consistency. Finally, it will switch to a mobile viewport to re-evaluate tap targets and layout constraints flagged as risks.
assumptions: The application is a Single Page Application (SPA) where navigation updates the DOM dynamically rather than loading new HTML files.
The 'Account' tab contains the entry point for 'Settings' and 'Privacy' configurations.
The '3 🔔' notification badge implies an interactive notification center or message list.
risk_hotspots: Notification Bell (ux-1): 38x38px tap target is below the 44px mobile accessibility standard.
'See all' link (ux-6): 42x16px text link is difficult to tap accurately on mobile.
Privacy Controls: Potential lack of clear feedback when toggling sensitive privacy settings.
Transaction Inputs: Validation logic for 'Send' amounts and addresses.

phases.title: Home & Navigation Baseline
phases.objective: Validate the initial state, status bar simulation, and global navigation integrity.
key_checks: Verify Status Bar elements (time, battery, wifi) are visible and static/simulated correctly.
Click each Tab Bar item (Home, Send, Receive, Activity, Account) to ensure screen transitions occur without error.
Inspect the 'Total Balance' card for visual hierarchy and clarity.
exit_criteria: All 5 tabs have been visited and returned to Home.
No console errors triggered during navigation.

phases.title: Account & Privacy Flow (Primary Goal)
phases.objective: Deep dive into the Account section to find and test Privacy/Settings controls.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Account' tab.
Locate 'Settings' or 'Privacy' menu items.
Toggle any available privacy switches (e.g., 'Hide Balance', 'Biometric Login').
Validate that state changes persist visually or provide immediate feedback.
Check for 'Log Out' or 'Support' adjacent links.
exit_criteria: Privacy settings located and interacted with.
User understands how to modify privacy preferences.

phases.title: Core Transactional Paths
phases.objective: Exercise the 'Send' and 'Receive' features to check input validation and flow logic.
key_checks: Click 'Send': Verify recipient input field and amount entry UI.
Attempt to submit empty or invalid data to check for error handling.
Click 'Receive': Verify QR code generation or address display.
Check for 'Copy Address' functionality.
exit_criteria: Send and Receive screens rendered successfully.
Input fields respond to interaction (focus states, keyboard appearance simulation).

phases.title: Activity & Notifications
phases.objective: Review transaction history details and notification interactions.
key_checks: Click 'See all' in Recent Activity (noting the small tap target risk).
Verify the full Activity list loads.
Click the Notification Bell (ux-1) to view the 3 pending notifications.
Dismiss or interact with a notification item.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport & Accessibility Audit
phases.objective: Repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/12 dimensions) to validate prescan warnings.
key_checks: Resize viewport to ~390x844.
Re-test tapping the Notification Bell (ux-1) and 'See all' (ux-6) to confirm difficulty/usability issues.
Check for horizontal scrolling or layout breakage in the 'Your Assets' list.
Verify bottom tab bar does not obscure content near the home indicator area.
exit_criteria: Layout remains intact on mobile width.
Usability issues with small tap targets confirmed via manual interaction attempt.

coverage_targets.features: Tab navigation, Privacy toggles, Send/Receive inputs, Notification drawer, Activity list
coverage_targets.mobile: Full regression of Phases 1-4 on mobile viewport, specifically targeting touch precision

notes: Since this is a single HTML file, 'page loads' are actually DOM manipulations. Wait for animations/transitions to complete before interacting.
Pay close attention to the 'small_tap_target' warnings in the prescan; these are high-priority UX critiques for the final report.
If 'Privacy' is nested deeply within 'Settings', document the click depth required to reach it.

findings.user_goal: Initiate a money transfer with valid inputs.
findings.problem: The application allows users to enter transaction amounts significantly higher than their available balance ($203M vs $5,820) without providing any immediate visual error, warning, or disabled state on the 'Continue' button.
findings.evidence: In the final observation, the display shows '$ 203,456,789' while 'Available $5,820.16' is visible above. The 'Continue →' button remains visually active (dark blue), implying the action is possible, which leads to user confusion upon submission failure.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of immediate validation creates a 'dead-end' interaction where users only discover the error after attempting to proceed, wasting time and reducing trust in the system's intelligence.
findings.suggestion: Implement real-time validation that disables the 'Continue' button and displays an inline error message (e.g., 'Insufficient funds') when the entered amount exceeds the available balance.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Send money screen, Amount display vs Available balance

findings.problem: The quick-select amount chips ($20, $50, $100, Max) have a height of only 25px, which is significantly below the recommended 44px minimum for mobile touch targets.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in the DOM summary identify targets ux-14 through ux-17 with heights of 25px. This small vertical hit area increases the likelihood of missed taps or accidental adjacent selections on touch devices.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets cause frustration and require precise motor control, which is difficult for users on the go or with larger fingers, violating basic mobile accessibility standards.
findings.suggestion: Increase the height of the quick-select chips to at least 44px, or add invisible padding around the buttons to expand the clickable area without altering the visual design.

findings.user_goal: Navigate back or access QR code features.
findings.problem: Header navigation controls (Back arrow and QR button) have tap targets smaller than the 44px guideline (36x36px and 45x30px respectively).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag ux-12 (Back) and ux-13 (QR) as small tap targets. The QR button is particularly narrow vertically (30px).
findings.why_it_matters: Header controls are primary navigation elements. If they are difficult to tap, users may struggle to exit screens or access secondary functions, leading to feelings of being 'stuck' in the app.
findings.suggestion: Expand the touch bounds of the header icons to 44x44px while keeping the icon visual size consistent.

findings.user_goal: Understand the status of the recipient selection.
findings.problem: The 'Continue' button appears enabled even when no specific recipient avatar is highlighted, relying on implicit text search or default states.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes that clicking 'Continue' without explicit avatar selection resulted in no state change or error, yet the button remained visually active. The UI does not clearly distinguish between 'search typed' and 'recipient selected'.
findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous selection states make it unclear whether the system has registered the intended recipient, causing hesitation before pressing 'Continue'.
findings.suggestion: Visually highlight the selected recipient avatar or clearly indicate in the search bar that a valid recipient has been chosen before enabling the primary action.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Recipient list and Continue button state
